clue.text: Between harbour and island, thin defensive barrier.

parts.note: a port is a harbour town or haven for ships
to cull is to thin out a herd or flock

explanation.surface: A thin barrier stands guard between a harbour and an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between harbour and island' places the thinning word between PORT and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle gateway's heavy grille, dropped to block attackers, is the classic fortified barrier.

clue.text: Carry too far out of Dover twice

indicators.note: the answer is lifted out of the doubled town name, so its outer letters are discarded
the word Dover is to be written two times in a row before the letters are taken

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel port, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes something too far by leaving Dover twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: Write DOVERDOVER; 'out of' lifts the six-letter answer from inside it, dropping the opening D and the closing VER.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry something too far is to exaggerate or overcook it, going beyond reasonable limits.

clue.text: Ducks partly reversed spiral dive

indicators.note: the two parts of the duck word swap ends, so only part order is turned round

parts.note: pintails are a kind of long-tailed dabbling duck

explanation.surface: Ducks, half turned about, plunge into a spiral dive.
explanation.walkthrough: PINTAILS is PIN + TAILS; 'partly reversed' swaps those parts round.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft spinning steeply downward in a corkscrew path is in this kind of plunge.

clue.text: Careless as Louis VI, for example

definitions.meaning: the French king Louis VI was called the Fat, so he was a king who was not thin

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as UN-THIN KING: Louis VI of France was known as Louis the Fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless conduct lacks thought; and Louis VI, nicknamed the Fat, was a monarch far from slim, read as un-thin king.

clue.text: Archbishop appears to strike a little woman

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit hard
Beth is one of the four March sisters in the novel Little Women

explanation.surface: An archbishop seems to hit a small woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambeth Palace in London is the official residence of the Archbishop of Canterbury, so the place name stands for the office.
explanation.definitionFit: By metonymy the London palace stands for Canterbury's primate, as the residence names its occupant.

clue.text: Pass resort, or several of them

indicators.note: to re-sort the letters is to sort them again into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountain pass resort, or perhaps a few of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort; 'them' refers back to resorts, the definition being several health resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Several resorts, specifically mineral-water towns, are wells for health cures.

clue.text: Hebe the flower girl

definitions.meaning: hebe is a shrub genus once classed within speedwells
a girl's name that is also the name of a blue-flowered plant, speedwell

explanation.definitionFit: Hebe shrubs were once placed in the speedwell genus, and the speedwell plant's name is also a girl's name.

clue.text: Launch preparation's. taken about a year in part of Ireland

indicators.note: the launch word is wrapped round the year letter, so it is taken around it

parts.note: the countdown is the sequence of numbers before a rocket launch
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a launch took a year in an Irish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken about' wraps COUNTDOWN round Y. Down is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, an Irish region.

clue.text: After long run, nothing goes right for playwright

parts.note: to pine is to long for something
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: After a long run with nothing going right, a dramatist suffers.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Wing Pinero was an English playwright of the late Victorian era.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Pinero wrote stage farces such as The Magistrate, so he is a dramatist.

clue.text: One by one, armies get destroyed without its backing

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters surround the other piece
being destroyed breaks up the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backing means turning back, so the letters of it run the other way

parts.note: its read as it's, it is, gives the word it

explanation.surface: One after another, armies are wiped out without support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get destroyed' turns ARMIES into SERIAM; 'backing' turns IT into TI; 'without' (outside) puts SERIAM round TI.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin adverb means in a series, taking points one after another in order.

clue.text: Certainly not noble?

parts.note: a noble was an old English gold coin, and a debased or counterfeit coin is the opposite of noble in both senses

explanation.walkthrough: The noble was a medieval English gold coin; its opposite, in metal and in morals, is a base one.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfeit piece of money made of inferior metal is ignoble, and the noble was a gold coin.

clue.text: High deck required for river work

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A high deck is needed for river work.
explanation.walkthrough: The poop is the raised deck at a ship's stern.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the raised stern deck is the topmost one, above the main deck.

clue.text: Supplement adding minimal amount to trip's cost, possibly

parts.note: P, a penny, is the smallest amount of British money

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged in some other way

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive letter included
taken as written

explanation.surface: An addition puts a tiny sum onto what a trip might cost.
explanation.walkthrough: P (a penny, the smallest British coin) leads; 'possibly' rearranges TRIPS + COST into OSTSCRIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A note added after a letter's signature is an addendum, a supplementary piece.

clue.text: Person of distinction rather than talent

parts.note: rather than can be read as not, as in this not that
talent is natural ability

explanation.surface: A distinguished figure owes it to something other than talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable or celebrated individual is a figure of note, someone eminent.

clue.text: Ask for some cricket, for starters.

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
an innings is a team's or batter's turn at batting in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone requests a spell of cricket to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is one side's turn at batting in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Starts or openings of anything are its origins, the first stages.

clue.text: Replacement for player's not out after partnership

indicators.note: after places the not-out word behind the partnership word

parts.note: in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batters
a batter who is not out is still in

explanation.surface: A substitute comes on for a cricketer who is not out after a long partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stand is a partnership at the crease, and a batter not out is still IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An understudy or substitute takes a performer's place when needed.

clue.text: Publicized drink in part of Yorkshire

parts.note: aired means made public, broadcast
ale is beer, a drink

explanation.surface: A drink is promoted in a Yorkshire district.
explanation.walkthrough: Airedale is the valley of the River Aire in Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The valley of the River Aire is a dale in that northern English county.

clue.text: A belligerent opener in test at the' Oval scored frantically

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, a fighter

indicators.note: the first letter of the word test opens it

parts.note: taken as written
the letter O is oval in shape

explanation.surface: A combative opening batter at The Oval scored runs at a frantic pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' means written in a musical score. The Oval is a London cricket ground, but here O is just its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical direction tells players to perform in an agitated, restless manner.

clue.text: Will writer analyse a story's. contents?

parts.note: to test something is to analyse or examine it

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters without the outer pair

explanation.surface: Is a will-maker studying the inside of a story?
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' keeps the inside of STORY, TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes a will to dispose of property after death is the legal term for a testator.

clue.text: Fame achieved by 26

definitions.meaning: the answer at 26 is a twin who was placed among the stars, as a star in Gemini

explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity status is renown; Pollux, made a star in Gemini, attained star status literally.

clue.text: Shattering in pieces — ordered' to tidy up

indicators.note: something broken in pieces is smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Having smashed something to pieces, someone is told to tidy up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' breaks SHATTERING up, and 'ordered' hints the fragments are put back in a fresh order.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order is to neaten them, which is to tidy.

clue.text: Pair entering into partnership at early stage

indicators.note: the pair goes inside the partnership, so it enters into it

parts.note: in bridge South and North play as partners
in cricket a pair is two ducks, two scores of nought

explanation.surface: Two people enter into a partnership at an early stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricketer out for nought in both innings bags a pair, two O's. South and North form a bridge partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortly, before long, at an early point is what the adverb means.

clue.text: French works left out, of their gallery, and English included

indicators.note: the English letter is put inside the trimmed gallery name
out means the left letter is dropped from the gallery name

parts.note: the Louvre is the French national gallery in Paris

explanation.surface: French artworks are left out of their gallery, with English ones included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' drops L from LOUVRE, leaving OUVRE; 'included' puts E inside after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word for work denotes an artist's whole body of output.

clue.text: Composer visibly embarrassed player

parts.note: someone visibly embarrassed goes red in the face
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A musician-writer was visibly embarrassed by a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer' looks musical, but it means one who puts a text together, an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor who puts text into shape for publication compiles it, an older sense of composing.

clue.text: Rechabite dragging in former, spouse as subject for sermon

indicators.note: the teetotal letters pull the spouse word inside them

parts.note: Rechabites were a temperance society, so a Rechabite is teetotal, TT
an ex is a former husband or wife

explanation.surface: A teetotaller hauls in an ex-partner as material for a sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: TT means teetotal; the Rechabites were a temperance friendly society.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher bases a sermon on a Bible passage, the verse chosen as its theme.

clue.text: Perform, having natural gift

parts.note: to do is to perform
native means natural, inborn

explanation.surface: Someone performs, endowed with natural talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gift' looks like talent following 'natural', but it is the definition: a donation.
explanation.definitionFit: A donative is a donation or present, especially an official largesse.

clue.text: Votes union leader in — he's just one of the, brothers

definitions.text: he's just one of the, brothers

indicators.note: the union's leading letter is placed inside the voting letters

parts.note: a poll is a counting of votes, and an X is the cross marking a vote
a poll is a counting of votes, and an X is the cross marking a vote

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Votes bring a union boss in; he is only one of the brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pollux and Castor were the twin brothers of Greek myth, the Dioscuri.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor's twin in Greek myth, one of the two Dioscuri sons of Leda.

clue.text: 'e trims, ever changing

indicators.note: changing means the letters alter their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Cockney says he trims, ever changing his views.
explanation.walkthrough: To trim is to shift opinions to suit the times, which is what such an opportunist does.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunist who adapts views to whatever is in fashion trims his sails to the prevailing wind.
